Developmental delay, intellectual disability and sensorineural deafness define the syndrome.
Inherited neurotransmitter metabolic disorder causing dystonia; structural foot deformities reported in 30-79%. Oculogyric crises reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Progressive myoclonic epilepsy with cognitive decline and motor degeneration; Lafora deposits alone do not establish damage to other organs.

Clonal histiocytic neoplasm; multisystem disease commonly infiltrates bone (~70%), skin (~50%) and liver (~30%). Pituitary involvement omitted at cap.
Cardiac septal defects and skeletal abnormalities with reduced bone density occur in 80-99%; hydronephrosis in 30-79%. Dental and nail findings omitted at cap.

Immune-mediated eosinophilic inflammation directly affects lung tissue; reactive blood eosinophilia does not establish a separate haematologic disease.
Skeletal dysplasia with core sensory/autonomic dysfunction; visual dysfunction occurs in 80-99%. Respiratory and feeding symptoms do not establish direct lung or GI damage.
Precursor B-cell leukemia/lymphoma affects blood and marrow; its explicit lymphoblastic lymphoma classification supports the immune axis.
Mucinous adenocarcinoma originates in the colon.
Substance dependence is excluded as a psychiatric disorder; organ toxicity is not intrinsic across this umbrella concept.
Inherited neutrophil functional defect impairs phagocyte antimicrobial activity; no common direct damage to other organs is established.
Localized plasma-cell neoplasm; osseous lesions account for roughly 65-80% of cases. Upper airway disease predominates only within the smaller extramedullary subgroup.
Adenocarcinoma originates in glandular epithelium of the colon.
Purely psychiatric psychotic disorder; no qualifying organ damage is part of its definition.
Complement C8 deficiency is an immunodeficiency. Meningitis and lupus are separate diseases, not direct organ involvement of the deficiency.
Congenital diaphragm muscle defect; associated lung hypoplasia from prenatal compression affects most patients. Herniated bowel alone does not establish GI damage.
Congenital cardiac outflow and great-vessel malformation; pulmonary hypoplasia and edema are reported in only 5-29%.
Axonal peripheral neuropathy; muscle atrophy in 20/29, pes cavus in 23/29, kyphoscoliosis in 17/29 and ankle contractures in 14/29 establish musculoskeletal damage.
Congenital cataracts, severe neonatal liver disease and global developmental impairment define the syndrome.
Progressive central and peripheral neurodegeneration; skeletal muscle atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Ophthalmoplegia and nystagmus reflect neurologic dysfunction.
